sentences.text: Researchers compared swallowing test results from times when patients were on their medication versus times when they were not, finding that the timing of the test relative to medication significantly changed the scores for bedside screens, video swallow studies, and dietary advice.

Bedside swallowing screen scores were better when tests happened during the medication's effective window, while doctors more often suggested changing liquid food textures when the video swallow study was done outside the medication window.
The authors note that because the study design was observational, they cannot prove that the medication itself causes the changes in swallowing.
